Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the grace days before a payout is chased, the deposit share of a direct booking, the weekly and monthly discounts and the wanted direct share.
Check Units, Channels, Cities and Team. They hold your units, the platform fees and payout days, the local tax percent of each city and the people the other sheets look up.
Enter every stay on Bookings with its channel, dates, rate, cleaning fee, local tax and status. The platform fee, the net payout, the payout date and the net per night calculate themselves.
Enter each payout on Payouts with the expected date and amount and what arrived. Days late, short amount and the chase flag show which payouts need a message today.
Record each chase on Payout Chase Log with the answer received, and each cancellation on Cancellations with the amount kept and the refund.
Keep Direct Deposits for direct bookings: the deposit, the balance and its due date, with overdue balances flagged red.
Use Check-in Calendar for arrivals and Same-Day Turnovers for days with a check-out and a check-in in one unit. Booking Changes and Booking Notes keep the history of each stay.
Read Channel Months and Fee Schedule to see what each channel costs, and Local Tax Lines for the tax collected and the tax the host must remit. Check your own local rules.
Use the 14 calculators for quotes, payout checks, fee comparison, cancellations, double bookings, forecasts, deposits, local tax, long stays and claims.
Read the Bookings Dashboard and Charts every week: bookings, gross, fees, net payouts, cancellations, late payouts and the direct share.
See which units earn, which lag and what to do about it
Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR by unit and month
every unit and month shows nights sold, the average price of a night sold and revenue per available night against the target for that unit
occupancy, ADR, rating and margin become one score out of 100 and name the weakest part of a unit
nights on the books now and a month ago against the nights wanted, with the gap and the price move to make for each unit and coming month
Occupancy needed for a revenue goal
a revenue goal and an ADR become the occupancy you must reach, and tell you if the goal is realistic
a price cut shows the extra occupancy needed to earn the same profit and whether the response you expect pays for it
every blocked period shows the revenue it cost at the ADR and occupancy of that unit, so owner stays and repairs are priced
occupancy, rate against the market, rating, lead time and weekday gaps point to the likely cause and the fix to try first
your occupancy, ADR and RevPAR against comparable listings by city and month, with the index and a fair share check
occupancy by weekday and unit shows the cheapest nights to fill and what they are worth in a year
nights and revenue against a year earlier split into more nights and a better rate, so you know what drove the change

One row per unit and month: available and booked nights and room revenue; occupancy, ADR (the average price of a night sold), RevPAR (revenue per available night) and the gap to target fill in.
Units with results of the last 12 months
One row per unit: type, city, owner, base rate and cleaner; nights, revenue, occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, the rank this month and the target checks fill in by themselves.
Bookings with ADR, lead time and rate against base
One row per booking: unit, guest, channel, dates, nightly rate and room revenue; the lead time, the ADR of the stay and the rate against the unit base rate fill in by themselves.
Twelve calendar months with the season and the price factor against the base rate; the season planner and the season plan read these.
Pace of nights on the books against the target
One row per unit and coming month: nights booked a month ago and now against the nights wanted by now; the pickup, the gap, occupancy on the books and the price move fill in by themselves.
Blocked nights with the revenue they cost
One row per blocked period: unit, dates and reason; the nights, the estimated revenue lost at the unit ADR and occupancy, and whether the block is long or current fill in by themselves.
Targets by unit with the result against them
One row per unit: wanted occupancy, wanted ADR and the yearly revenue goal; the target RevPAR, the results of 12 months against each target and the share of the goal reached fill in by themselves.
City months with occupancy, ADR and RevPAR
One row per city and month, added up from all units there: available and booked nights and room revenue; occupancy, ADR and RevPAR fill in by themselves.
Unit type months with occupancy, ADR and RevPAR
One row per unit type and month, added up from all units of that type: nights, room revenue, occupancy, ADR and RevPAR; the type with the best RevPAR shows in the charts.
Weekday pattern of nights slept by unit
One row per unit and weekday over the last 12 months: nights available, nights sold and room revenue; occupancy, ADR and the gap to the unit average show which nights are cheapest to fill.
Lead time curve: bookings by how far ahead they were made
One row per check-in month and lead time bucket: bookings, nights and revenue; the average stay, the ADR and the share of the month fill in by themselves.
Year on year by unit and month
One row per unit and month with nights and revenue this year and a year earlier; the change in nights, revenue and ADR and the trend fill in by themselves.
Orphan nights: free nights between two bookings
One row per free night or short gap between two bookings: unit, date, length and whether it was filled; the revenue missed at the unit ADR and the fill check fill in by themselves.
Review scores by unit and month
One row per unit and month-end: reviews and the average rating of the last 90 days; the rating band and the check against your minimum rating fill in by themselves.
Channel mix by unit over 12 months
One row per unit and channel over the last 12 months: nights sold and room revenue; the share of the unit nights, the ADR and the main channel check fill in by themselves.
City and season with local occupancy tax
One row per city and season: local occupancy tax (a tax on each night, collected from the guest) and a demand factor; the occupancy and ADR of your units there fill in by themselves.
Length of stay mix by unit over 12 months
One row per unit and stay length bucket over the last 12 months: bookings, nights and room revenue; the share of nights, the ADR and the revenue per booking fill in by themselves.
Performance reviews with findings and actions
One row per finding on a unit: what was found, the action, who owns it, the due date and when it was done; the status, the days to the due date and the unit results fill in by themselves.
Competitor set summary: our results against the market
One row per city and month: the occupancy and ADR of comparable listings from your own market checks; our own results come from City Months, with the indexes and the checks.
Team with the review actions owned
The host, the co-host (a helper who handles guests for a fee), four cleaners, two handypeople and four outside contacts; the review actions each person owns fill in by themselves.
